chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Za'farani narrated to me in Ray, saying: Yahya ibn Sulayman narrated to us from Abdullah ibn Uthman ibn Khaytham from Sa'id ibn Abi Rashid from Ya'la ibn Murrah, who said:
The Messenger of Allah (s.a.a.w.) said: Husayn is from me and I am from Husayn. Allah loves those who love Husayn. Husayn is a chief (seed/offspring) from among the chiefs.

key_terms.حُسَيْنٌ: Husayn, the grandson of the Prophet
key_terms.سِبْطٌ: Chief, seed, or offspring (often used for Imams)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the phrase 'Husayn is from me and I am from Husayn' in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith, recorded in *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, articulates the ontological unity between the Prophet and Imam Husayn through the phrase 'Husayn minni wa ana min Husayn,' affirming his status as a 'Sibt' (descendant/chief) from the twelve Sibtun mentioned in Surah Al-An'am. It underscores the Shia doctrine that love for the Ahl al-Bayt is not merely a social virtue but a criterion for divine pleasure, linking the spiritual authority of the Imams directly to the Prophet's essence.
